card.name: Nouns completing 'in/on/at' adverbial phrases
card.fires_on: The noun that ends a short hedging phrase after a preposition, such as 'on average', 'in principle', 'in most cases', 'in turn', 'in general', 'at times'. It also fires on 'well' in 'could well'.

modes.label: on average
modes.description: The word 'average' after 'on', introducing a typical figure or amount.

modes.label: in principle / in general / in turn
modes.description: An abstract noun that completes 'in ...' as a sentence-level qualifier.
modes.example: Aid, too, can in<< principle>> enhance countries' competitiveness and provide growth,

modes.label: in most cases / at times
modes.description: A noun that closes a frequency or extent phrase before the main verb or a dose change.
modes.example: the maintenance dose of lamotrigine tablets will in most<< cases>> need to be decreased by as much as
